Cold kitchens slow fermentation, so Gerald and your dough need more warmth and time. Here’s how to keep your weekend loaves rising well:

- Wake Gerald before bake day
  - 1–2 days ahead, pull him from the fridge and give 2–3 warm feeds (1:2:2 or 1:3:3, a spoon of rye helps). Use 80–85°F water and keep him around 75–80°F. Use at peak when he doubles in 4–6 hours and smells sweet/tangy.

- Hit a warm final dough temperature
  - Target 24–26°C (75–79°F) after mixing. Use warmer mix water to get there and check with a quick thermometer.

- Create a warm proofing spot
  - Turned-off oven with the light on, microwave with a mug of hot water, or a cooler with a hot water bottle/heating pad on low. Aim to keep the dough itself ~75–80°F.

- Lengthen bulk and go by signs, not the clock
  - Expect bulk to take 1.5–2× longer in winter. End bulk when the dough is smoother, jiggly, with visible edge bubbles and ~50–75% rise.

- Final proof smartly
  - After shaping, give 30–90 min at room temp (poke test: slow, gentle spring-back), then cold retard 8–16 hours. If your fridge is very cold, give 30–60 min at room temp before baking.

- Weekend schedule (fits a morning person)
  - Thu evening: take Gerald out, warm feed.
  - Fri morning: warm feed; Fri evening: build levain.
  - Sat morning (9–10 AM): mix to 24–26°C, bulk warm 4–6 h with a couple folds early. Shape late afternoon, brief bench proof, then into the fridge.
  - Sun morning: bake straight from the fridge.

- If you need insurance
  - Add a tiny pinch of instant yeast (0.1–0.2% flour weight: ~0.5–1 g per 500 g flour). It boosts rise without killing sourdough character.

- Between bakes
  - Store Gerald a bit stiffer (50–60% hydration) in the fridge to keep him robust, and always give two warm feeds before baking.

- Scapegoat for additional static analysis (optional but useful)

SBT wiring (team-wide)

Configs to commit
- .scalafmt.conf:
  - runner.dialect = scala213 or scala3 (match your version)
  - maxColumn = 100 or 120 (pick one and stick to it)
  - trailingCommas = always
  - newlines.source = keep (or classic) based on preference
- .scalafix.conf (baseline rules):
  - rules = [OrganizeImports, RemoveUnused, DisableSyntax]
  - DisableSyntax: disallow var, return, null (tune to taste)
  - For Scala 2.13, rely on RemoveUnused to clean imports; for Scala 3, you can also surface -Wunused via compiler if desired.

- IDE: Enable “Use scalafmt” in IntelliJ’s Scala plugin and format on save. Avoid IDE-specific import formatting; let scalafix OrganizeImports handle it.

CI enforcement (fail fast)
- sbt scalafmtCheckAll
- sbt "scalafixAll --check"
- sbt test
- sbt scapegoat (optional; publish HTML report as an artifact)

Team policy tips
- One .scalafmt.conf at repo root; no per-module overrides unless unavoidable.
- Treat CI warnings from linters as errors, but keep the ruleset small at first (OrganizeImports, RemoveUnused, a few DisableSyntax bans), then ratchet up.

3) Rotation cadence and fairness
- Cadence: 1-week blocks, Monday 09:00 to Monday 09:00 [local time].
- Round‑robin across eligible team members; new hires join after completing onboarding (see Training).
- Limits:
  - Max 1 consecutive week on-call.
  - Min 2 weeks between weekend duties.
  - No one holds more than 6 weeks of on-call per year without opt‑in.
- Holidays: Evenly distributed; if one person covers a major holiday this cycle, they get priority to skip the next.
- Time zones: Rotate so late-night burden is shared across time zones where applicable.
- Swap rules: Allowed with mutual agreement; submit at least 48 hours in advance and update the schedule/tool. Inside 48 hours, Lead approval required.

- Sev‑1 (critical outage, security issue, widespread data loss):

  - Customer update cadence: every 30 minutes until stable, then hourly

  - Engage: 30 minutes
  - Customer updates: hourly until resolved or workaround
- Sev‑3 (moderate impact; standard escalations):
  - Acknowledge: 1 hour during business hours; next business day if overnight
  - Customer updates: daily or as per case SLA

- Primary (P1):
  - Monitors paging system and escalation channels.
  - Triage severity, start mitigation/runbook, loop in P2/DM/Engineering as needed.
  - Log actions and timeline in the ticket/incident record.
  - Ensure customer-facing updates meet cadence above.
- Secondary (P2):
  - Joins for Sev‑1/Sev‑2 or if P1 requests support.

  - Coordinates roles, stakeholder comms, and post-incident follow-up for Sev‑1/Sev‑2.

Before you get in (2–3 minutes, optional but helpful for the shoulder)
- Band work: external rotations, rows, Y/T/W, 10 reps each, slow and pain‑free.

Day 1 – Technique + Easy Aerobic (≈25–30 min, ~700–900 m)
- Warm-up: 2×50 easy choice with fins, 15–20 s rest
- Drills: 4×25 catch-up with snorkel, 15 s rest
- Main: 6×50 freestyle as 25 easy/25 moderate, 20–30 s rest
  • If the shoulder twinges, swap every other rep to backstroke
- Kick: 4×50 flutter kick with board or on side, 20 s rest (use fins if you like)
- Cooldown: 1×100 very easy back/free mix

Day 2 – Endurance Intervals (≈20–25 min, ~600–700 m)
- Warm-up: 4×25 easy free with snorkel, 15 s rest
- Main ladder: 25–50–75–100–75–50–25 (total 400 m) at RPE 5–6
  • Rest 20–30 s after 25/50; 30–45 s after 75/100
  • Use fins on the 75/100 if the shoulder feels taxed
- Easy pull: 4×25 with pull buoy, gentle catch, 15 s rest (no paddles)
- Cooldown: 1×50 easy

Day 3 – Low-Shoulder Focus + Drills (≈25–30 min, ~700–800 m)
- Warm-up: 4×25 easy backstroke or snorkel free, 15 s rest
- Main: 8×50 as 25 kick + 25 relaxed free with fins, 20 s rest
- Drill set: 6×25 single‑arm free with fins/snorkel (alternate arms), 15 s rest
  • If anything pinches, switch to side‑kick drill instead
- Cooldown: 1×100 easy

Day 4 – Continuous Build + Aqua Jog Option (≈20–30 min, ~600–900 m)
- Warm-up: 2×50 easy, 15–20 s rest
- Main: 10–15 min continuous as 25 free / 25 back alternating
  • Use snorkel and/or fins to keep it shoulder‑friendly
  • If needed, break into 50s with 10–15 s rest
- Optional: 5–10 min deep‑water running (belt) for extra cardio, zero shoulder load
- Cooldown: 2×50 very easy

Progression (4–6 weeks)
- Add 1–2 reps to the 50s each week or trim rest by 5 s.
- Grow the continuous segment by 2–3 minutes weekly (cap ~20–25 min).
- Keep effort mostly RPE 5–7. No sharp pain; stop or switch strokes if the shoulder complains.

Shoulder and asthma notes
- Avoid paddles and butterfly; keep pull‑buoy work light and brief.
- A center‑mount snorkel reduces neck/shoulder rotation; fins shift some load to the legs.
- Keep inhaler/nebulizer poolside. Use interval rest as needed; take 30–60 s extra if you feel tight or wheezy.

answer:
Great default pattern: give each new feature its own supervision subtree that isolates failures, gives you per-entity workers, and keeps transient work separate.

Suggested layout
- Feature.Supervisor (strategy: :one_for_one)
  - Feature.Registry (Registry, keys: :unique, partitions: System.schedulers_online())
  - Feature.DynamicSupervisor (DynamicSupervisor, strategy: :one_for_one, max_children as needed)
  - Feature.TaskSupervisor (Task.Supervisor for short-lived jobs)
  - Optional: Feature.Cache (GenServer/ETS), RateLimiter/CircuitBreaker

Why this works
- Crash isolation: one worker crash won’t take siblings down.
- Easy per-entity routing: Registry gives you stable pids by id.
- Scalable fan-out: DynamicSupervisor starts only what you need, when you need it.
- Separation of concerns: Task.Supervisor handles transient async work.

Minimal wiring (plain Elixir)
children = [
  {Registry, keys: :unique, name: Feature.Registry, partitions: System.schedulers_online()},
  {DynamicSupervisor, name: Feature.DynamicSupervisor, strategy: :one_for_one},
  {Task.Supervisor, name: Feature.TaskSupervisor}
]
Supervisor.start_link(children, strategy: :one_for_one, name: Feature.Supervisor)

Start/find per-entity workers
- Name via Registry: {:via, Registry, {Feature.Registry, id}}
- Start under DynamicSupervisor with restart: :transient
- One helper to “ensure” a worker exists:
  def ensure_worker(id) do
    case Registry.lookup(Feature.Registry, id) do
      [{pid, _}] -> {:ok, pid}
      [] ->
        spec = %{
          id: {Feature.Worker, id},
          start: {Feature.Worker, :start_link, [[id: id, name: {:via, Registry, {Feature.Registry, id}}]]},
          restart: :transient,
          shutdown: 5_000
        }
        DynamicSupervisor.start_child(Feature.DynamicSupervisor, spec)
    end
  end

Worker outline
- Keep state minimal; push I/O retries/backoff into the worker.
- Use telemetry and defend external calls with timeouts and jittered retries.
- child_spec/1 returning restart: :transient is usually right.

When to vary the strategy
- Boot order dependencies (e.g., Connection -> Listener -> Processor):
  - Make a small sub-tree with strategy: :rest_for_one for those, so if Connection dies, dependents restart in order.
- Workflows needing backpressure or batching:
  - Prefer GenStage/Broadway instead of bare GenServers; supervise producers/consumers in a dedicated subtree.
- Very high scale routing:
  - Keep Registry partitioned (as above) or shard by key into multiple DynamicSupervisors.
- Pools to cap concurrency:
  - Use Task.Supervisor.async_stream_nolink with max_concurrency, or set max_children on DynamicSupervisor.

Operational knobs to set
- Supervisor intensity/period to prevent restart storms (e.g., max_restarts: 3, max_seconds: 5).
- Conservative shutdowns (5–10s) for external I/O teardown.
- Timeouts on calls (GenServer.call/3) and external clients.
- Telemetry events on starts/stops/crashes to observe the tree.

Here’s a quick, safe way to lift velvet pile on crushed seat cushions:

- Tools: lint roller or rubber glove, upholstery vacuum (brush attachment), handheld steamer (or kettle steam), soft clothes/velvet brush or clean microfiber cloth.
- Prep: Remove pet hair/debris first, then lightly vacuum with the brush tool.
- Find the nap: Stroke the fabric to see which way looks darker/smoother. You’ll lift against it, then finish with it.
- Steam lightly: Hold the steamer 6–12 inches away and pass quickly so the fabric gets warm and just slightly damp—don’t soak.
- Brush the pile up: While warm, use short, gentle strokes to lift against the nap; then do a final pass with the nap for an even sheen.
- Let it dry fully before sitting.

For stubborn shiny pressure marks: place a barely damp microfiber cloth over the spot and steam through the cloth, then brush as above. Use distilled water (especially for cotton/silk velvet) and test in a hidden area.

Avoid: direct ironing, heavy pressure, soaking, or fabric shavers. For prevention, rotate/flip cushions, stand them on edge to “air,” and use a throw where your cat prefers to sit.
